case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 12.11.2014, passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2700 of 2012)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 12.11.2014, passed by the High. Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2700 of 2012 discharging the Rule arising out of judgment and decree dated 11.044.2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikgonj, in Title Appeal No. 27 of 2011 reversing the judgment and decree dated 16.1.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Harirampur, Manikgonj in Title Suit No. 196 of 2007 dismissing the suit.

<u>2. Facts leading to filing of this civil petition for leave to appeal in short are that the present respondents No. 1 and 2 as plain-tiffs instituted Title Suit No. 271 of 2006 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikgonj, for declaration of their title, on the basis of purchase of the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint and also for declaration that RS record in respect of the said land is wrong. Subsequently the said suit being transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, Harirampur, Manikganj, renumbered as Title Suit No. 1.96 of 2007. It is stated that 0.26 acre of land of C.S. Khatian No. 90 corresponding to C.S. plot No. under mouja Binodpur Borokhando, Singair, Manikgonj originally belonged Lc Ghetu Pramanik in 8(eight) annas shares, Hcrinhok- a Pramanik in 4 annas share and Tenu Praman 1A in share; that while in possession Ghetu Pramanik died leaving behind 3 sons namely, Juran, Hridoy and Kurani who inherited the same; that thereafter Hridoy plod leaving behind one son, Nitai; and Kurani died leaving behind one daughter, Monisha; that subsequently, pursuant to amicable settlement between the parties, Juran became the owner of .15 acre of land and Nitai and Monisha together became the owners of .11 acre of land; that Juran transferred his .15 acre of land to Haldar Mondal who died leaving behind two sons, namely, Kutu Mondal and Dudu Mondal and as such they became the owners of .15 acre of land; that subsequently, said Kutu. Mondal and Dudu Mondal transferred their 0.15 acre of land in favour of one Gafur and handed over possession of the same who in his turn transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 1 vide kabala No. 4111. dated 09.10.1986 in equal share; that Nitai and Monisha also transferred 0.10 out of 0.11 acre of land in favour of plaintiff No.1 vide kabala No. 11990 dated 18.11.1972 and subsequently on 01.12.1972 they also transferred the rest 0.01 acre of land in favour of plaintiff No.1 by unregistered document as the value of the same was below Tk.100.00 but the Plaintiffs are owning and possessing the said 0.10 acre from Gafur and 0.11 acre from Nitai and Monisha total 0.21 acre of land by purchase; that in the end of Ashaar, 1413 B.S. when the plaintiffs went to pay rents they came to know that out of 0.15 acre of land purchased from Gafur only 0.08 acre of land has been recorded in their names in RS Khatian No. 351 in place of 0.10 and .10 acre of land has been recorded in the name of defendant No.1, Abdul Ali, in R.S. Khatian No. 516 in place of 0.05 acre of land and out of 0.11 acre of land purchased from Nitai and Monisha only 0.08 acre of land has been recorded in the name of Plaintiff No.1 Jinnot Ali; hence the suit.</u>

3. Defendant No. 2 contested the suit, by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that, the suit land along with other lands measuring 0.26 acre originally belonged to Ghetu Pramanik in 8 annas share, Horibhokta Pramanik in 4 annas share and Tenu Pramanik in 4 annas share; that on the basis of amicable partition, Ghetu Pramanik became the owner of 0.26 acre of land and as such while possessing the same, Ghetu Pramanik died leaving behind three sons namely Juran, Hridoy and Kurani as his heirs; thereafter Hridoy died leaving behind his son Nitai and Kurani died leaving behind his daughter Monisha; that Juran Mondal by amicable partition had been possessing the entire 0.26 acre of land out of which he transferred 0,13 acre along with 0.38 acre in RS Plot no. 219, 0.6 'A acre in RS Plot No. 185 and 0.38k acre in RS Plot No. 186 of Binodpur Boroldwido mouza in total .96 acre of land to Haider Mondal by registered kabala dated 23.02.1956; that Haider Mondal died leaving behind two sons namely, Kutu Mondal and Dudu Mondal and they transferred .15 acre, of the suit land along with acre out of .37 acre of land in SA Plot No. 185 and 0.45½ acre out of 0.88 acre of land in SA Plot No. 186, totalling .70 acre of land to defendant No.2; that the said defendant No.2 although purchased 0.15 acre of the suit land but he possessed the entire 0.26 acre of the suit land; that thereafter the defendant no.2 on 09.10.1986 transferred 0.15 acre; of land out of the suit land along with .11¼ acre of land from Plots no. 185 and 186 in total .26¼ acre of land to the plaintiffs and the defendant No.1; that the defendant no.1 obtained 0.10 acre of land in the western part of the suit land; that pursuant to amicable settlement RS record has been prepared and accordingly he is possessing the same upon erecting houses thereon; that the defendant No.2 is the owner and possessor of 0.08 acre of land situated in the eastern side adjacent to the 0.10 acre of land of the defendant No.1 on the western side which has been recorded in the RS record in his name; that on the basis of settlement the plaintiffs are possessing 0.08 acre on the eastern side of the suit land along with 0.09 acre of land in SA Plot No. 185 in total .17 acre of land which has been recorded in his name; that the RS record has not been prepared in the name of the defendant no.2; that the plain-tiff no.1 fraudulently got .44 acre of land of defendant no.2 in Plot no. 186 recorded in his name in RS Khatian No. 517, Plots No. 345 and 346 and erected some houses in some portion of the same forcibly and dispossessed the defendants; that the plaintiff no.1 expressed about the purchase of .10 acre of land from Nitai and Monisha on 18.11.1972 but had no possession over the same; that Ni tai Left for India during Pakistan regime; that the plaintiffs on false personation fraudulently created the deed by which no title vested upon him and, as such, the suit is not maintainable; hence the suit should be dismissed.

4. The Trial Court, upon hearing, dis-missed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 16.01.2011, against which, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal. No.27 of 2011 before the learned District Judge, Manikganj, which was ultimately heard and allowed by the learned joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj, and thereby decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 11.4.2012.

5. Against the said judgment and decree, the defendant No.2 moved the High Court Division in Civil. Revision No. 2700 of 2012 and obtained Rule. On the other hand, the defendant No.1 also moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2415 of 2012 and obtained Rule.

6. A Division Bench of the High Court Division heard both the Rules together and upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record discharged both the Rules by its judgment and order dated 12.11.2014.

7. Hence defendant No.2 filed this civil petition for leave, to appeal against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2700 of 2012.

<u>8. Mr. A.S.M Khalaquzzaman, learned advocate appearing for the defendant No.2-petitioner submits that Court Division committed error of law in dis-charginc7 Rule without giving its independent findings. He that when the plain-tiff no.1, as PW 1, admitted in cross examination that the defendant no.1 had been possess:- the western .10 acre of land of the suit plot by erecting houses thereon and that the plaintiffs had boon possessing the eastern 0.08 acre of the suit plot, it is clear that the plaintiffs have failed to prove their possession in their claimed 0.21 acre of land of the suit plot and, as such, the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division committed error in decreeing the suit without discussing the material points resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He also submits that the plaintiffs upon forging and by false personating somebody as Nitai and Monisha created the deed fraudulently and as such by the said forged and fraudulent deed no title has been passed to the plaintiffs because the said Nitai and Monisha left for. India during Pakistan regime but the lower appellate Court as well as the High Court Division basing on the said forged and fraudulent deed passed the impugned judgment which is liable to be set aside.</u>

9. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, the learned Advocate-On-Record, appearing on behalf of the respondents supporting the impugned judgment submits that the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order and decreeing the suit.

10. It appears that admittedly the suit land measuring 0.26 acre of land, belonged to Ghetu Pramanik in 8 annas share, Horibhokta Pramanik in 4 annas share and Tenu Pramanik in 4 annas share. It is also admitted that on the basis of family settlement, Ghetu Pramanik became the 1.6 annas owner of 0.26 acre of land, who died leaving behind three sons namely Juran, Hridoy and Kurani as his heirs. It is also admitted that Hrioy died leaving behind only son Nitai and Kurani died leaving behind only daughter Monisha.

11. The plaintiffs claim that there was an amicable settlement between Nitai, Monisha and Juran, on the basis of which Juran became the owner of 0.15 acre of land and Nitai and Monisha together became the owners of 0.11 acre of land. On the other hand, the defendants claim that pursuant to the amicable partition, Juran got the entire 0.26 acre of land of the suit plot. In support of their respective claims and counter claims the plaintiffs adduced 1. Witness as PW 1 along lath papers which were marked as Exhibits 1 to 3 and the defendants adduced 1 witness as DW 1 along with papers Which were marked as Exhibits Ka to Umma.

12. The trial Court, while dismissing the suit held that the plaintiffs have proved their possession over 0.08 acre of land and failed to prove the same over rest of their claimed 0.21 acre of land. That is the plaintiffs have no possession over their entire claimed land. On perusal of the schedule to the plaint the trial Court observed that although the plaintiffs brought the suit claiming 0.20 acre of land but subsequently by amendment they have claimed 0.21 acres of land without correcting the descriptions by meets and bounds of the schedule and, as such, it observed that the schedule of the plaint being indistinct and indefinite the plain-tiffs have failed to prove their claim over the entire suit land.

13. The appellate Court, can the other hand, on perusal of the evidence adduced by the parties and the other materials on record, found that the plaintiffs have been in possession over 0.21 acre of land, after purch4sing the some from Nitai, Monisha and defendant No.2, for more than 30 to 40 years, Further on the question of possession over the said 0.21 acres land of the plaintiffs, DW 1. remained silent which indicates his admission about such possession of the plaintiffs. Thus it held that the plaintiffs' title and possession over their purchased 0.21 acre of land in the suit plot has been proved by the evidence of DW-1. Accordingly, the appellate Court came to the finding that the RS record in respect of the suit land is wrong and without any basis and the suit, is maintainable in its present form and manner and, as such, the plaintiffs are entitled to get relief as prayed for and thereby decreed the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

14. The High Court Division, upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, found that Court of appeal below rightly considered deed No. 11990, dated 18.11.1972 by which Nitai and Monisha transferred .10 acre of land to the plaintiffs, though the defendants claimed that the said deed is forged and fraudulent as Nitaj and Monisha left for India during Pakistan regime which they miserably failed to prove further held that subsequently Njtai and Monishaalsc-transferred the rest .01 are of land to plaintiff. No.1 which was not registered as the valuation of the same; was less than TK.100/=, even than it cannot be said that the said .01 acre of land has not been transferred the plaintiffs. It also found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their possession in the suit land since purchase for more than 30 to 40 years and accordingly, it held that the deed being more than 30 years old, the same has the presumptive value as per section 90 of the Evidence Act. In addition to the aforesaid 0.11 acre of land purchased from Nitai and Monisha the High Court Division upon considering deed No. 4111. dated 9.10.1986(Exhibit-2) also found that 0.15 acre of land have been transferred by Abdul Gafur in favour of plaintiffs no. 1 and 2 and defendant no. 1 . Thus, the High Court Division found that PWs 1, 2 and 3 proved possession of the -plaintiffs in their claimed land and also held that there may be minor discrepancy in their depositions but that itself is not sufficient to hold that it vitiated plaintiffs' case of possession and accordingly discharged the Rules by the impugned judgment and order.

<u>15. From the above discussion and on perusal of record it further appears that, the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division believed the plaintiffs' case and disbelieved the claim of the defendants as to the forgery of the deed of Nitai and Monisha rather, held that since the defendants failed to prove their claims that Nitai and Monisha left Bangladesh for India during Pakistan time by sufficient evidence and since the deed is more than 30 years old it has got the presumptive value under section 90 of the Evidence Act.</u>

16. From the submission of Mr. Khalequgzaman it appears that the main contention of the defendants is that Nitaiwhom the plaintiffs claimed to be one of the owners has left the Country for India during Pakistan regime and the plaintiffs by false personation created deed No. 11990 dated 18.11.1972. But it appears that the questioned deed was in the custody of the plaintiffs who submitted the same in the trial Court and proved and marked as Exhibit-3. On the other hand the defendants failed to prove their claim of forgery and false personation by adducing sufficient evidence. Moreover the said registered deed being more than thirty years old it has sufficient presumptive value under section 90 of the Evidence Act.

<u>17. Regarding possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land on the basis of the said deeds, the DW 1 remained silent in reply to the quaries rather than to dislodge its .presumptive value, when he was asked about the same. This has led the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division to come to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have possession, title and interest in the suit land.</u>

<u>18. In the case of Syed Abdul Haque Vs. Surendra. Nath Majumder, reported in 59 DLR(AD) 111 this Division held "since the documents exhibits 1 and 2 are 30 years old and have a presumption of correctness and that presumption having not been dislodged by the defendants there was no occasion for the Court to discard the claim of title of the plaintiffs made on the basis of the said documents." This Division in the case of Bangladesh Railway Vs. Jashimuddin, reported in 5 LM(AD)58 held. "from- the discussions made herein above since the plaintiffs have been successful in proving their genealogy of title and possession in the suit land and since the defendants failed to challenge the documents relied upon by the plaintiffs and also failed to prove their case of title and possession, it can clearly be held that the defendants have no title and possession in the suit land. On the other hand the plaintiffs could prove the title of Yeasin Hazi, the CS recorded tenant and thereafter devolution of title and possession upon his daughter Duburunnessa who in her turn transferred the same to Khodeza Begum by two registered documents in 1955 and 1956 which are more than 30 years old documents and relying on such registered documents Khodeza Begum's name being recorded in the SA record and thereafter Zumuruddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs having purchased the same got his name mutated in place of Khodeza Begum in the office of the Government, and after his death his heirs, the plaintiffs having got, their names mutated, the title and possession of the plaintiffs are found to be proved".</u>

<u>19. In the instant case, the plaintiffs claimed the suit land on the strength of Deed No. 11990 dated 18.11.1972 from the Nitai and Monisha which is more than 30 years old document and produced by the plaintiffs during trial without being dislodged by the defendants nor the same has been challenged by the defendants in any Court there is no scope to discard the Claim of the plaintiffs' title on the suit land on the basis of the said deed. The trial Court on perusal of the said deed (Exhibit-3) found that the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from Nitai and Monisha, but it misdirected itself in coming to the conclusion that the plaintiffs are in possession of 0.08 acre of land and the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, and, as such, held that the suit is not maintainable.</u>

20. It further appears upon scanning all the evidence on record that the Court of appeal below rightly reversed the findings of the trial Court and the High Court Division was also correct in affirming the same and, 4s such, it did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment and thereby decreeing the suit.

21. The aforesaid findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being based on proper appreciation of law and fact the same does not call for any interference by this Court.

22. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
